name: Labels outside Google: Fontsource, Fontshare, the four libre foundries (Velvetyne, Collletttivo, Tunera, Use & Modify), Font Squirrel, DaFont and other curated directories
what_it_is: What each source actually hands us as data. (1) Fontsource API (api.fontsource.org/v1/fonts): per family id, family, subsets, weights, styles, defSubset, variable, lastModified, category (sans-serif, serif, display, handwriting, monospace, icons), licence, type. No tags, no mood, no description. (2) Fontshare API (api.fontshare.com/v2/fonts): 100 families in one response (count_total 100, has_more false); per family font_tags (use cases such as Magazines, Books, Posters, Logos), category, a 'story' paragraph (median 166 words, 100 of 100 non-empty), designers, license_type (itf_ffl). (3) Use & Modify (usemodify.com): no API; each family page lists keywords from a fixed 48-word menu (1900, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2010, 2020, ascii, bitmap, blackletter, code, curveless, cyrillic, damage, derivated, didone, extended/wide, gaelic, garalde/old face, generative, geometric, glyphic/incise, graphic, grotesque/lineale, humanist, inktraps, large character map, latex, mechanistic, monolinear, monospace, narrow, organic, paleographic, pixel, reverse-contrast, revival, rounded, sans serif, screen, script, serif, slab, smallsize, super-family, symbols, variable, wonky). Pages carry no description text, only keywords. (4) Collletttivo: no machine-readable labels at the source we use (its GitHub org lists 18 repos, 1 with a description, 1 with topics). Its website shows a small tag set (see catalog_coverage) but its robots.txt disallows AI crawlers, so it was not fetched. (5) Tunera: the cached homepage (server/.cache/tunera/home.html) has cards only, no filters or tags; Crawl-delay 10. (6) Velvetyne: GitLab METADATA.yml/FONTINFO.json plus GitLab topics, which the app already reads; velvetyne.fr was never requested. (7) Font Squirrel: a documented JSON API (/api/classifications, /api/fontlist/all, /api/fontlist/{name}) with genre-style classifications; today it answers plain clients with HTTP 202 and an empty body (bot challenge), so not usable politely. (8) DaFont: 9 top-level categories and 72 subcategories (Fancy 18, Foreign Look 6, Techno 4 (Square, LCD, Sci-fi, Various), Bitmap 1, Gothic 5, Basic 4, Script 8, Dingbats 21, Holiday 5); look/genre labels, no mood or motion category (the only sport item is Dingbats > Sport, which is symbols, not letters). (9) Other curated directories: Open Foundry (human-curated display of open-source fonts, no structured mood tags found) and FontLibrary.org (6,000+ fonts organised by licence). Source of the counts: measured by me from server/.cache/remote-v7.json, server/data/*.json, server/.cache/usemodify/*.html, and the scratchpad fontsource.json and fontshare.json.
provider_and_url: Fontsource: https://fontsource.org/docs/api/fontlist and https://api.fontsource.org/v1/fonts . Fontshare (Indian Type Foundry): https://www.fontshare.com , API https://api.fontshare.com/v2/fonts (undocumented). Use & Modify (Raphael Bastide): https://usemodify.com , about page https://usemodify.com/about/ . Collletttivo: https://www.collletttivo.it/typefaces , GitHub org https://github.com/collletttivo . Tunera: https://www.tunera.xyz . Velvetyne: GitLab group https://gitlab.com/velvetyne (site velvetyne.fr deliberately not touched). Font Squirrel: https://www.fontsquirrel.com/blog/2010/12/the-font-squirrel-api . DaFont: https://www.dafont.com/themes.php . Open Foundry: https://open-foundry.com/about . FontLibrary: https://fontlibrary.org/en/catalogue .
catalog_coverage: Counted by me by re-running the app's mergeSources rules (priority velvetyne, collletttivo, tunera, fontsource, fontshare, usemodify; Noto and Playwrite excluded) in Python over remote-v7.json plus server/data/*.json; result 2,099 rows, matching the brief. Saved at scratchpad merged_catalog_other.json. Rows with no Google tags: 339 = Velvetyne 63 + Collletttivo 26 + Tunera 23 + Use & Modify 163 + Fontshare 64 (this is the brief's '~340'). FONTSOURCE: 1,760 of 1,760 Google rows have a category (Fontsource's own count for Google-type entries: sans-serif 730, display 478, handwriting 360, serif 352, monospace 52, icons 8, of 1,980); 0 of 1,760 get a mood from Fontsource. Current Google-derived tags in the catalog (context for the gap): 137 rows have none, 376 have 1 or 2, average 3.8 per row. FONTSHARE: 64 of 64 rows have tags (average 4.6) but all are use-case words (tag counts across the 64 rows: Magazines 44, Books 34, Poster 25, Posters 23, Logos 21, Editorial 21, Websites 17, Branding 15, Banners 12). 'story' text exists for 64 of 64 (100 of 100 in the API) but is not stored in the app's cache today. 35 further Fontshare families are already Google rows (alsoOn fontshare). USE & MODIFY: 163 of 163 rows have tags (average 3.4); 53 rows have 2 or fewer. Cached family pages: 191, of which 8 carry no keyword at all (average 3.3 keywords per page). COLLLETTTIVO: 26 of 26 rows tagged (average 7.6), but by hand from rendered specimens in server/sources/collletttivo.ts, not from the source. A search-result snippet of the site's own tag set (Free, Display, Geometric, Playful, Extreme, Sans, Text, Elegant, Folk, Serif, Variable, Monospaced, Slab; 16 typefaces) is [uncertain]: I did not fetch the site. TUNERA: 23 of 23 tagged (average 7.4), hand-written the same way. VELVETYNE: 63 of 63 tagged (average 6.6), partly from metadata files/topics, mostly curated in server/sources/velvetyne.ts. FONT SQUIRREL, DAFONT, OPEN FOUNDRY, FONTLIBRARY: 0 rows labelled; no overlap with our six sources was measured, because none could be fetched politely or none offers per-font labels. Correction to the brief: the 339 indie and Fontshare rows are not untagged. They carry tags, but in vocabularies that share almost nothing with Google's mood words (see vocabulary_alignment).
granularity: Per family everywhere. Fontsource lists weights and styles as arrays with no per-style labels; Fontshare tags apply to the family. Indie rows are the app's rows, which are a family or a named variant (for example Ampoule Neon and Ampoule Neon Tube, or Collletttivo width variants such as Condensed and Wide), and variants can have their own hand-written tags. No source labels the italic or any variable-axis position.
signal_type: Mostly structure, genre, era and use case, not semantic mood. Fontshare = use cases. Use & Modify = form words, eras and curator slang (wonky, damage, generative, mechanistic, curveless). Collletttivo, Tunera and Velvetyne (as written in this app) mix form words with a few mood words (elegant, playful, quirky, techno, cyberpunk). DaFont and Font Squirrel = genre taxonomies.
mood_dimensions_covered: All counts are rows among the 339 non-Google rows, measured by me over the merged catalog (scratchpad merged_catalog_other.json). MOTION / ACTIVE: almost nothing. Only 4 of 339 rows carry a direct motion or lean word: Anthony ('leaning'), Sporting Grotesque ('sporty'), Azabache ('streamlined', 'slanted'), Nippo ('Jerseys', 'Sports'). Use & Modify has 0 of 48 keywords about speed. DaFont has no motion category. Fontshare 'story' text helps a little: with a strict word list (dynamic, sport, athletic, speed, fast, energy, motion, racing) 8 of 100 stories match, 6 of them for rows in our catalog (Tanker, Neco, Kola say 'dynamic'; Roundo, Nippo, Hoover say sports or athletics). For contrast, 89 of 1,760 Google rows carry the Active tag. LOUD / HEAVY: indirect only. Velvetyne 10 rows, Collletttivo 3 and Tunera 3 carry heavy, bold, punchy, poster, headline or titling; Use & Modify 0. Fontshare has 51 of 64 rows with Poster, Posters, Headline(s) or Banners use-case tags, which say 'set large', not 'loud'. CALM: Velvetyne 2, Collletttivo 3, Tunera 1 (Paysage 'calm'), Use & Modify 0, Fontshare 0. FUTURISTIC / TECHNO: the best covered of the mood words. Velvetyne 10 rows (futuristic 2, technical 2, computer 4, techno 1, industrial 1, mechanistic 1), Tunera 6 (techno 4, cyberpunk 4, neon 4, all on the Ampoule rows), Collletttivo 2 (technical), Use & Modify 21 (mechanistic 10, code 9, screen 4; these are form keywords, not moods). Fontshare 0 mood-like; 7 rows carry the use-case tags Code, Screen, Programming or Monospaced. ELEGANT: Collletttivo 11 of 26 rows (elegant on 9; also luxury, delicate, fashion), Velvetyne 7 (elegant on 6), Tunera 3, Use & Modify 0, Fontshare 0 (one 'Fashion' use-case tag). HANDMADE: Use & Modify 45 (wonky 33, damage 15), Velvetyne 12, Tunera 8 (hand-painted, brush), Collletttivo 1. PLAYFUL: Velvetyne 15, Collletttivo 6, Tunera 5, Fontshare 5, Use & Modify 0. Net: these catalogs can express form, era and a little techno, elegant, handmade and playful; they cannot express speed or action.
query_style_specificity: Helps more for loose or structural requests ('wonky', 'monospace', 'pixel', 'blackletter', 'elegant serif', 'poster') than for tight mood or motion requests ('fast', 'action'), where the vocabulary is nearly empty. The only tight-mood words with real coverage are techno/futuristic (39 rows across Velvetyne, Collletttivo, Tunera and Use & Modify, of which 21 are Use & Modify form keywords) and elegant (21 rows across Collletttivo, Velvetyne and Tunera).
quality_evidence: None of these sources publishes any validation for mood or motion queries. What I can offer is my own count (mood_dimensions_covered): a 'fast / action' request can match by tag at most 4 of the 339 non-Google rows, plus 6 Fontshare rows by story text; the model has to infer the rest from letterforms it cannot see. No test was run through server/vibe.ts (no real searches were spent). The Fontshare story field is the one genuinely informative text signal found: a designer-written paragraph per family, for example Nippo and Hoover are described with athletics and sports words. Source for the Fontshare numbers: https://api.fontshare.com/v2/fonts response saved in the scratchpad (fontshare.json); regex counts by me.
known_noise: Fontshare tags: spelling variants of one idea (Poster 25 vs Posters 23, Logo vs Logos, Headline vs Headlines), one family tagged with another font's name ('Poppins'), and use-case words that say nothing about shape. Fontshare story text: a loose motion regex matches 18 of 100 stories, but most are 'rhythm' or 'quick' (reading rhythm, quick to read); the strict regex gives 8 of 100, two of which (Khand, Karma) are not Fontshare rows in our catalog. Use & Modify: the site does not define its keywords (about page), and some slugs differ from their labels (amateur is shown as wonky, modified-fork as derivated). Collletttivo, Tunera and Velvetyne tags in the catalog are an earlier session's reading of rendered specimens; error rate not measured [uncertain]. Font Squirrel classification names come from a search-result summary (Blackletter, Calligraphic, Comic, Dingbat, Display, Grunge, Handdrawn, Monospaced, Novelty, Pixel, Programming, Retro, Sans Serif, Script, Serif, Slab Serif, Stencil, Typewriter) [uncertain].
name_and_memory_bias: The 339 non-Google families are mostly unknown to the model, so only their tags carry information, and evocative names (Sporting Grotesque, Tanker, Nippo, Hoover, Ampoule Neon, Malebolge) can sway a pick more than the letters do. The prompt already tells the model to avoid 'very common' fonts and lists the independent rows first (band order in compactCatalog), so a thin label set shows up as noisy picks rather than as silence. Google rows suffer the opposite bias: the model remembers popular ones.
untagged_rows: No non-Google row is untagged today, so nothing is silently dropped for lack of tags. The unfairness is vocabulary: the model must translate 'fast' into each source's own words. The bigger silent gap is on the Google side: 137 of 1,760 rows have no tag and 376 have only 1 or 2. Inside the indie group, 53 Use & Modify rows have 2 or fewer tags.
text_interference_risk: Not applicable: these are text labels, nothing is rendered.
integration_path: Almost nothing new to integrate: the labels are already in the catalog as the tags field, and compactCatalog in server/vibe.ts (line 358) prints them. Three small, optional additions, in order of value: (1) Fontshare story: add the story field to the remote rows in server/catalog.ts build(), but do not send the paragraph; condense it offline into one 'looks like' sentence and store it in a precomputed file such as server/data/looks.json, format { "<family lower-case>": "one sentence" } (this overlaps the designer-descriptions item). (2) A synonym table in INSTRUCTIONS that maps request words onto each source's vocabulary, format JSON word -> tags[], for example 'fast, action, speed' -> italic, slanted, leaning, sporty, streamlined, condensed, sharp, angular, heavy, Active, Excited, Loud, dynamic, techno. About 300 to 500 tokens once, cacheable. (3) A scoring step before the model: count how many of a row's tags fall in the expanded set (plain code), shortlist about 150 rows (independent rows first), then let the model rank the shortlist. Same data format as (2). Font Squirrel, DaFont, Open Foundry and FontLibrary: do not integrate.
tokens_per_row: Zero extra for what exists. Current catalog rows measure about 17 to 30 tokens each (characters divided by 3.6, my estimate: Velvetyne 26, Collletttivo 30, Tunera 28, Fontsource 21, Fontshare 20, Use & Modify 18); the whole catalog text is about 161,000 characters, roughly 45,000 tokens. A one-sentence Fontshare note would add about 15 to 25 tokens on 64 rows (about 1,000 to 1,600 tokens in total). The synonym table adds 300 to 500 once. All of it is static, so the prompt cache keeps working.
vocabulary_alignment: Adds new terms; barely maps onto Google's. Measured by me against Google's 20 Expressive tag names (Active, Artistic, Awkward, Business, Calm, Childlike, Competent, Cute, Excited, Fancy, Futuristic, Happy, Innovative, Loud, Playful, Rugged, Sincere, Sophisticated, Stiff, Vintage): rows carrying one of those exact words are Velvetyne 9 of 63 (playful 7, futuristic 2), Collletttivo 1 of 26, Tunera 2 of 23, Use & Modify 0 of 163, Fontshare 0 of 64. Adding Google's Theme words (pixel, blackletter, stencil, techno, brush...) lifts Velvetyne to 25, Tunera to 12, Use & Modify to 20 (almost all 'pixel'), Collletttivo to 3, Fontshare to 1. Against the 200 most frequent MyFonts tags (a separate research item), indie vocabularies overlap much more: Velvetyne 52 of its 159 distinct tags, Collletttivo 34 of 73, Tunera 34 of 91, Use & Modify 15 of 45, Fontshare 22 of 53.
explainability: Yes, a match can quote the tag or the Fontshare story sentence. For indie rows it can also say the tag was hand-written from specimens.
determinism: The labels are fixed data, so a tag-scoring step before the model is deterministic. The model stage is not.
build_effort: Keeping the current labels: zero. Adding Fontshare story to the cache and a looks.json: about half a day for an agent (one change in server/catalog.ts, one offline batch, a unit test that every Fontshare row has a note). Synonym table plus tag-count shortlist: about one day including a 20-query smoke test. Integrating Font Squirrel or DaFont: not worth building (see risks).
per_search_cost_and_latency: None added for stored labels and the synonym table (a few hundred extra cached prompt tokens). A pre-model shortlist step is plain code, milliseconds.
one_off_cost: About 100 families from one Fontshare API call (already in the scratchpad, so no new fetch). An offline condensing batch for 64 stories is one small claude -p run. No other downloads.
human_effort: Reviewing the synonym table: about 1 hour. If a person later adds motion words to the 339 non-Google rows by hand, the brief's 30 seconds per font gives about 2.8 hours once, then about 30 seconds per new family.
asset_access: Fontsource: open API and jsDelivr CDN files, fetched daily by the app. Fontshare: the scratchpad copy of the API response (pulled by the framework agent, not by me) holds all 100 families; font files are on cdn.fontshare.com. Use & Modify: HTML pages fetched by the app at 0.6 s spacing and cached under server/.cache/usemodify (robots.txt returns 404, so no rules). Collletttivo: its robots.txt blocks GPTBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, CCBot and others with Disallow /, so the app reads GitHub and jsDelivr only. Tunera: crawl delay 10, the app makes one homepage request per week and reads font files from the repositories. Velvetyne: velvetyne.fr opts out of AI agents; the app uses GitLab's API (and GitHub through jsDelivr). Font Squirrel: documented API, but both robots.txt and /api/classifications answered HTTP 202 with an empty body to a plain curl and WebFetch returned nothing, which looks like a bot challenge; I stopped after one attempt each. DaFont: robots.txt allows theme pages and disallows dl.php, /download/, search.php; it has no API; I made one page view of themes.php.
licence_and_provenance: Fontsource: packaging MIT, fonts under their own licences (mostly OFL); metadata derived from Google's. Fontshare: ITF Free Font License (itf_ffl): personal and commercial use and web embedding are free, redistribution and modified redistribution are not allowed (from secondary sources: abduzeedo.com, madegooddesigns.com) [uncertain, the licence page itself loaded only as a tagline]; so rendering specimen images for a private search index is probably fine, but this is not OFL and should be checked before any derived image is published. Use & Modify: every listed font is libre (OFL or similar); the site states no licence for its keyword data and the selection is Raphael Bastide's personal taste. Collletttivo and Tunera: OFL fonts. Velvetyne: mostly OFL. DaFont: mixed licences per font (free for personal use, demo, donationware, 100% free, public domain/GPL/OFL), so it is not a catalogue of fonts free for commercial use. Font Squirrel: curated as free for commercial use but its terms were not readable.
etiquette: Never velvetyne.fr (not requested). Collletttivo's site blocks AI crawlers (not requested). Tunera crawl delay 10. Use & Modify 0.6 s gaps in the app. DaFont and Font Squirrel: no scraping; Font Squirrel is bot-protected. Fontshare and Fontsource APIs: one call each, cached.
maintenance_and_freshness: Fontsource lastModified is current and the app refetches daily (24 h TTL in server/catalog.ts). Fontshare is a closed set of 100 families, nearly static. Use & Modify index is refreshed weekly by the app. The hand-written tags for Collletttivo, Tunera and Velvetyne need a person or a model to write tags for each new family and variant (npm run sources rebuilds rows; new families without a hint entry fall back to metadata tags or none).
risks_and_limitations: These sources cannot answer motion or loud/calm queries, so adding more of them will not fix 'fast movement'. DaFont and Font Squirrel add genre labels we mostly have, with licence and bot-protection costs. The brief's premise 'indie fonts have few or no tags' is wrong in the narrow sense (0 of 339 are untagged) and right in the useful sense (their vocabulary does not meet the request words). Some counts rest on blunt word lists (my regexes) and on tags an earlier session wrote, so a different word list would move them a little. Collletttivo's own tags and Font Squirrel's classification names are unverified.
evaluation_hook: Coverage test, no model needed: take 25 mood and motion request words, expand each with the synonym table, and report for every source the share of rows matched (today 'fast' reaches 4 of 339 non-Google rows by tag). Then run the 25 requests through vibe.ts before and after the table and have a person rate the result grids.
recommendation_for_font_explorer: Use partly, as small plumbing; skip as a source of moods. (1) Keep Fontsource category, Fontshare tags, Use & Modify keywords and the hand-written indie tags exactly as they are. (2) Add one thing from this group: the Fontshare story, condensed offline to one sentence per family (64 rows) and merged into the designer-descriptions item. (3) Add a synonym table that translates request words into the indie and Fontshare vocabularies, since that, not missing tags, is the real mismatch. (4) Skip Font Squirrel, DaFont, Open Foundry and FontLibrary: no mood data, licence mess, and Font Squirrel is bot-protected. (5) For motion, look at the measured-traits and vision-labels items; the 339 rows need new signal, not more labels of this kind. Relative to the other items, this one is the weakest source of new signal and the cheapest to finish. Smallest first step: write the synonym table for the 10 most useful request words (fast, action, loud, calm, techno, elegant, handmade, playful, heavy, retro) and run the coverage test above.
